name: CLIP
plain: CLIP image encoders from OpenAI and OpenCLIP (LAION-2B, DataComp-XL, DFN; B, L, H): image features aligned with text.
summary: CLIP image towers (Radford et al. 2021): OpenAI, OpenCLIP (LAION-2B, DataComp-1B) and Apple DFN weights in timm's format; cls + patch tokens at any size, pooler_output = the post-LayerNorm cls token before the projection (QuickGELU for the OpenAI and DFN weights).

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
Reproducible scaling laws for contrastive language-image learning
DataComp: In search of the next generation of multimodal datasets

official.reason: timm re-implements the CLIP image towers and hosts the OpenAI, OpenCLIP and DFN weights in one format; the authors' packages carry the text towers and their own APIs.
timm re-implements the CLIP image towers and hosts the OpenAI, OpenCLIP and DFN weights in one format; the authors' packages carry the text towers and their own APIs.

limitations: kernels replays a CUDA graph per small input shape without hidden states (up to about 1M activations: ViT-B ~460 px, ViT-L ~300 px), captured on the shape's second call, at most 4 per model; `model.release_graphs()` frees them.

Small kernels calls (graph-sized, with or without `layers`) run GEMMs of at most 600 tokens on cuBLAS: faster in a graph replay (ViT-B/16 224 px: 1.26 against 1.52 ms), about 10 % slower eagerly on ViT-T / B; a replay equals the eager call bit for bit.
`fp32_accumulate = true` puts every GEMM on cuBLAS with fp32 accumulation (the portable precision; slower on GeForce).

fp16 error against the fp32 original is higher than for the other ViTs on L/14 DataComp (mean 2.8 % portable, 4.8 % kernels): one residual channel sits near 120, where fp16 steps are 0.06, about 10 % of the median activation. No overflow; float32 portable gives 0.3 %.

DFN weights: the relative error (mean 1.3-3.9 % portable, 3.9-6.5 % kernels) is measured against a median |output| of only 0.015-0.021 (other weights: 0.5-0.6) with values up to 0.7; `fp32_accumulate = true` lowers kernels to about 1.5 %.
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: dense patch features and a pooled image feature.
